plan.opening_note: My notes say the small rewrites in field.rs (shift-add reduction, masked sub, limb unrolls) did not move field_arith_ir, and that the inverse is the likely hotspot. So this time I'll read the bench and invert_canonical first rather than retry those edits.

hypotheses: My notes say the small rewrites in field.rs (shift-add reduction, masked sub, limb unrolls) did not move field_arith_ir, and that the inverse is the likely hotspot. So this time I'll read the bench and invert_canonical first rather than retry those edits.
Squaring alone measured 0.9901, just short of the 0.9900 gate. An earlier masked-borrow sub measured about 0.9956 by itself, so I'm adding it on top.
Combining the two came out worse (0.9959) than squaring alone, so I'm reverting the sub change. Next I'll try doubling the off-diagonal words with an add chain instead of shifts.
The add-chain doubling did worse (0.9988), so I'm going back to shifts. Before using my last evaluation, I'll look at invert_canonical for one more saving.

actions.reason: secp256r1/src/field.rs: montgomery_square used to build the 512-bit square column by column with u128 accumulators and manual overflow counters. It now computes the six off-diagonal products once with a mac chain, doubles them with one-bit shifts across the limbs, and adds the four diagonal squares in a single carry chain. In montgomery_reduce_words, each multiply-accumulate x * MODULUS[1] + x is replaced by its exact equivalent x * 2^32 (a new add_shl32 helper), since MODULUS[1] = 2^32 - 1. Results are the same values. Equivalence outputs are identical, all tests pass, field_arith_ir ratio is 0.9899 and scalar_arith_ir is unchanged.
